items.title: Item 1
items.text: Zscaler Tumbles 20% as Guidance Disappoints *********************************************** Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS ) fell over 20% ahead of the market open after results indicated a slower pace of growth going forward. Weak revenue guidance for the coming quarter – partly due to lower demand in Europe – and cuts to the full-year free cash flow margin contributed to the fall. * “Zscaler is the cybersecurity platform for the AI era. This is evident in our results and the reason we are so confident in our long term potential”: CEO Jagtar Singh Chaudhry struck an upbeat tone, choosing to focus on the record non-GAAP profitability and strong recurring revenue as the company (lagging the S&P 500 by 76% since the Stock Advisor recommendation by Team Hidden Gems four years ago) continues to tap into AI capabilities. * “It's clearly a top dog in an important emerging industry”: Fool contributing analyst Toby Bordelon outlined the investment case for Zscaler back in March, saying it “enjoys a host of sustainable competitive advantages. Switching costs are significant for enterprise customers. The massive amount of data Zscaler receives as it processes traffic creates another advantage.” Watch Tom G interview Zscaler’s CEO -------------------------------

items.title: Item 2
items.text: Nvidia Ramps up Taiwan Spend ------------------------------- Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang confirmed the company will increase spending in Taiwan from $100 billion to $150 billion a year going forward, as he believes "Taiwan is the epicenter of the AI revolution." * "Four years ago, five years ago, Nvidia was spending about $10 [billion], $15 billion a year in Taiwan": The scale of increase in investment in the country has been significant, mostly due to the strong ecosystem it has regarding manufacturing semiconductors that Nvidia – and other big tech companies – use. * Pace of investment growth unlikely to slow for Nvidia: Huang’s comments come as Nvidia is building a new office in Taipei that can house 4,000 engineers, with further projects in the works. items.title: Item 3
items.text:
Amazon and Starlink Eye EU Orbit Bid --------------------------------------- Reuters reports Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN ) and Starlink will be able to bid and potentially acquire some European mobile satellite spectrum next year, in a move enabling further expansion in the sector for the respective companies. * European licenses a key piece of the puzzle: The satellite spectrum allows mobile devices and vehicles to communicate clearly even in remote locations, making access to it important for sector operators that want global scale. * Two-thirds of the spectrum is anticipated to be held for European companies: Despite the potential for Amazon and Starlink, the vast majority of licenses are likely to be granted to European peers. items.title: Item 4
items.text: Don’t Forget About Earnings From UHAL, HEI, and NTNX ******************************************************* As mentioned in yesterday's Breakfast News , today sees key earnings from Salesforce (NYSE:CRM ), Snowflake (NYSE:SNOW ), Synopsys (NASDAQ:SNPS ), and Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE ). A little more under the radar are the following companies, due to report after the closing bell. * U-Haul (NYSE:UHAL ) will be aiming to post a better set of results following the 94% drop in profit last quarter . Higher expenses triggered the fall, with management expecting the elevated costs to bottom out later this year for the Stock Advisor rec by Team Rule Breakers. * HEICO (NYSE:HEI ) is forecast to show double-digit year-over-year (YoY) gains in both revenue and earnings, as the Flight Support Group continues to benefit from higher demand, as noted last quarter . The company is recommended in Stock Advisor by Team Hidden Gems. * Nutanix (NASDAQ:NTNX ) is expected to deliver a 5.1% YoY revenue increase, building on the strong recurring revenue from last quarter , although concerns remain for the Rule Breakers rec about supply chain bottlenecks that caused management to lower full-year guidance. items.title: Item 5
items.text: Today’s Take: See You Next Month *********************************** Alicia Alfiere If I checked my portfolio only once a month, I’d make things as routine as possible and work to remove emotion from my process. I’d make a recurring calendar appointment and make sure that money for new investments already hit my account. Then, I’d consult my investing journal for companies and index funds to buy. — ALICIA ALFIERE • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Neha Chamaria That’s an easy question for me to answer, because I actually often don’t check my portfolio for weeks at a stretch. When I adopted this approach a couple of years ago, the biggest change was in my own temperament. I stopped looking for constant validation of my thesis, trying to find a reason behind a stock’s swings even when there was none. — NEHA CHAMARIA • TEAM HIDDEN GEMS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to reveal what you would do differently if you could only check your portfolio once a month, or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! See more in Today’s Take **************

items.title: Item 6
items.text: Your Take ************** YESTERDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked: How are you feeling about your current portfolio allocation as we end the month? Confident, cautious, or ready to make changes? E Member explodingrobots said “I need to diversify more. I'm so tech and AI heavy. It seems like most of the MF recs are tech and AI plays. Those are the sexiest and get most attention. Lately MF has been providing guidance on and recommending AI-proofing your portfolio and non-AI/tech stocks, in case of a big drawdown, which I really appreciate.” See more great answers from our Foolish community TODAY’S QUESTION What's one stock, sector, or trend you're watching more closely heading into next month?
